completionEvidence.description: Positive control: AGENT_IN_BOX_VM_STORAGE=%LOCALAPPDATA%\AgentInBox\space path test\vms (ASCII with spaces) passed one full TestQemuProviderIntegration round in 24.77s (Go test 24.69s, exit code 0), including create, start, login, restart reconciliation, idempotent start/stop, graceful stop and snapshot create/restore.

Negative result: AGENT_IN_BOX_VM_STORAGE=%LOCALAPPDATA%\AgentInBox\路径 测试\vms (Unicode + space) failed at QEMU start in 0.54s. The overlay was created and vm.json written, but qemu-system-x86_64 exited with 'cannot create PID file: Failed to create PID file' before QMP became available.

The same failure occurred on non-system drive D: with D:\路径 测试\vms; the drive letter is not the cause. Direct probes with correctly quoted QEMU arguments showed that -pidfile, -serial file: and -drive file= all fail to open paths containing Chinese characters, while the same ASCII path with spaces works. qemu-img itself can create and query the qcow2 overlay at the Unicode path.
QEMU stderr, vm.json and Go test output for the C: and D: Unicode path failures.

error.message: The MSYS2 QEMU 11.1.3 Windows build cannot open file paths containing non-ASCII characters (-pidfile, -serial and -drive all fail). The provider places qemu.pid, console.log and the overlay under the configured storage root, so a Unicode storage root cannot be started by this QEMU build.

notes: PRE-FIX FAILURE, kept as evidence. Custom storage with ASCII spaces was verified; custom storage containing Unicode failed on both C: and D: with QEMU 'cannot create PID file'. D: is a second partition on the same physical NVMe as C:, not a second physical disk; a separate physical disk remains untested. This result is superseded by 2026-11-10-h1-whpx-custom-storage-shortpath-fix.json, which implements GetShortPathNameW plus an ASCII junction fallback in internal/vmprovider and passes the same C:/D: Unicode tests. The Windows ANSI code page (Chinese CP936) makes QEMU's UTF-8 path bytes unusable for ANSI file APIs; enabling the Windows UTF-8 beta locale was not needed and was not tested.
